title: PhlimboV3._claimRewards phUSD mint leg (:863) is un-wrapped (no _tryTransfer+bank) -> a mint-authorization revocation reverts every stake/withdraw/claim and freezes principal
description: PhlimboV3._claimRewards:863 mints phUSD to the beneficiary inline (phUSD.mint(...)) and is NOT wrapped in the _tryTransfer+bank pattern used by the sibling stable leg (:876) and promo leg (:902). Story-029 closed V3-M-05's UNprivileged USDC-blocklist stable/promo vector by banking those legs, but left the phUSD mint leg un-wrapped. If phUSD mint authorization is revoked/paused for PhlimboV3 (e.g. the ecosystem-wide kill-switch phUSD.revokeAllMintPrivileges() or setMinter(PhlimboV3,false), typically pulled to contain an UNRELATED minter incident on the shared token), the mint reverts inline and reverts every staker's stake/withdraw/claim -- principal is frozen.
impact: Temporary denial of service on principal. No asset theft and no permanent loss: principal is fully recoverable -- the owner re-grants the mint role (unfreezes) or sweeps principal out-of-band via emergencyTransfer.
attackPath: 1. Owner/operator calls phUSD.revokeAllMintPrivileges() or setMinter(PhlimboV3,false) -- typically to contain an UNRELATED minter incident on the shared ecosystem token.
2. PhlimboV3._claimRewards:863 phUSD.mint(beneficiary,...) is not _tryTransfer+bank wrapped (unlike stable :876 and promo :902).
3. Every staker's stake/withdraw/claim reverts because the reward-claim leg reverts inline -- principal is frozen for ALL stakers simultaneously.
4. Recovery: owner re-grants mint authorization (unfreezes) or emergencyTransfer principal out-of-band.
likelihood: low -- requires a privileged authorization revocation on the shared phUSD token; there is NO unprivileged/permissionless trigger. The freeze is a non-obvious side effect of a global kill-switch, hence a Law-3 footgun; it cannot be induced by an external attacker.
severityRationale: Carried at Medium under the symmetry rule (borderline -> keep the higher severity, pending human triage). severity-classifier assessed Low (owner-privileged trigger with no unprivileged path + fully owner-reversible). severity-auditor assessed Medium: (a) blast radius is ALL stakers' principal frozen simultaneously -- broader than the Medium parent V3-M-05, whose USDC-blocklist trigger froze only an individual blocklisted beneficiary; (b) the trigger is an EXTERNAL shared-ecosystem-token authorization revocation that PhlimboV3 does not control, matching the C4 Medium bar 'protocol function/availability impacted, temporary fund freeze, with stated assumptions and external requirements'; (c) users cannot self-recover. Resolution: carried at the higher severity (Medium) per the symmetry rule, pending human triage via /ledger phlimbo-ea.

severityDispute.severityClassifier: Low -- trigger is owner-privileged (no unprivileged/permissionless path) and the freeze is fully owner-reversible with no asset loss; under C4 a DoS that requires a privileged action AND is recoverable by that same privilege is QA/Low.
severityDispute.severityAuditor: Medium -- invoked the symmetry rule (borderline -> keep higher + human triage). Blast radius = ALL stakers frozen at once (broader than the individual-beneficiary parent V3-M-05); the trigger is an EXTERNAL shared-token authorization revocation PhlimboV3 does not control (C4 'protocol availability impacted, temporary fund freeze, with external requirements' = Medium); users cannot self-recover.
severityDispute.resolution: Carried at the HIGHER severity (Medium) per the symmetry rule, pending human triage.

humanTriageQuestion: Is the phUSD/Flax mint authority the same trusted entity as PhlimboV3's owner, AND is revokeAllMintPrivileges() expected to be short-lived? If YES to both -> Low is defensible (self-inflicted, self-cured freeze). If the Flax authority is a separate ecosystem operator (as the mutable-dependency structure suggests) or the freeze is unbounded -> Medium is correct. The user can finalize via /ledger phlimbo-ea.
recommendation: Wrap the phUSD.mint leg at :863 in the same _tryTransfer+bank pattern as the stable (:876) and promo (:902) legs, so a mint-authorization revert defers the reward rather than reverting the whole stake/withdraw/claim path.
